name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply all safe changes immediately, then log the rest for review.

This keeps the improvement loop fast without waiting for human review on every tweak. The trade-off is accepting a small risk of bad changes slipping through—but we’ll catch them in the logged review, and the speed gains outweigh the risk.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t bad changes slipping through—it’s that "safe" is subjective until proven by a human. Auto-applying without clear, auditable criteria invites drift. Settle it by defining what "safe" means in measurable terms before automating.
